narrative.overview:
The system is a dark room with one screen awake. Most surfaces are near-black, flat, and separated by a single hairline; the terminal preview is the only object allowed to cast a deep shadow and a violet glow. The page should feel like a quiet desk at 1 a.m., not a product launch.

The voice is calm, nocturnal, and quietly playful. Mono type carries the interface and the headlines, so the page reads as software rather than a brochure. Avenir Next appears only for human explanation: the lede, section intros, card body, FAQ answers. That split keeps the terminal authority without making long prose feel like a changelog.

Color behaves like a spectrum, not a brand wash. Ultraviolet, hot pink, and peach are concentrated in the signal: the colored headline, the primary action, the visualizer, the live dots. The rest of the page stays in midnight, ink, muted grey, and one hairline violet. Motion is scarce. The spectrum, the pulsing live dot, and a one-pixel hover lift are the whole vocabulary.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black field with a faint violet and pink atmospheric wash.
Hairline-bordered instrument panels, not floating cards.
Mono for structure, sans for explanation.
One glowing terminal as the focal object.
Spectrum color concentrated in signal and action, never spread as page tint.
Still page; motion belongs to live data.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Only the terminal preview gets a deep shadow and a broad violet glow. Every other surface is flat with a hairline border. If a second object glows, the room is no longer dark.

rules.name: The Spectrum Is The Accent Rule
rules.body: Ultraviolet, hot pink, and peach belong to signal, action, and the headline accent. They never become a full-page background tint. Keep accent coverage under roughly 10% of any viewport.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Mono sets the interface, headlines, labels, code, and terminal content. Sans sets paragraphs a person reads. Never set a long paragraph in mono; never set a terminal label in sans.

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Large mono headings close their tracking (-0.03em to -0.045em) and sit near 1.0 line-height. Small mono labels open their tracking (+0.12em to +0.13em) and stay uppercase. The scale contrast is the hierarchy.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure comes from 1px #23233a borders and spacing, not from shadows or background fills. A panel should still read as a panel in grayscale.

rules.name: The Resolvable Hold Rule
rules.body: Any demo state that changes the whole page must expose an exit from anywhere. The fixed hold status bar, the demo button, and the hero toggle are the same exit at three distances.

dos: Do keep the page field at Midnight #07070e; use Panel Ink #0d0d18 for contained surfaces.
Do use 1px Hairline #23233a borders for all structure.
Do set headlines and interface labels in the mono stack, and long prose in Avenir Next or the system sans fallback.
Do keep the terminal as the only object with a deep shadow and broad glow.
Do concentrate ultraviolet, hot pink, and peach in the signal: colored headline, primary action, visualizer, live dots.
Do use real TUI screenshots, label demo-mode captures, and make every visible control work or name its scope.
Do preserve keyboard access, visible focus, and reduced-motion support.
Do keep a demo hold resolvable from anywhere on the page.
donts: Don't use pure black #000 or pure white #fff.
Don't give cards, panels, or buttons a drop shadow.
Don't wash whole sections in violet or pink gradients.
Don't use radii above 12px except the hero status pill.
Don't add scroll reveals, parallax, or ambient motion. Motion belongs to live data and state changes.
Don't set body paragraphs in mono or terminal labels in sans.
Don't invent testimonials, user counts, benchmarks, or product claims.
Don't advertise TUI shortcuts as working web controls.
